brief: A calendar showing energy levels — mornings are high ground, post-lunch dips are valleys

dominant_strengths: Inventive use of mini bar charts inside calendar cells turns abstract energy data into a scannable circadian rhythm pattern
Color encoding (green peak, amber medium, red valley) is intuitive and harmonizes with a clean neutral grid
Legend placement and naming (Peak/Valley) reinforce the topographical metaphor cleanly
dominant_weaknesses: Seven tiny bars per cell create visual noise; without hour labels or axis the chart is decorative more than legible
Date numerals are quiet and the bars dominate, making it hard to use this as an actual calendar for navigation
Repetition across 30+ near-identical cells flattens the insight—weekly or monthly patterns aren't surfaced
fix_priorities: Add subtle time-of-day axis or hover tooltip so each bar's meaning is recoverable
Strengthen date typography hierarchy and reduce bar saturation on out-of-month cells further
Introduce aggregation (weekly average row, or anomaly highlighting) so patterns emerge beyond per-cell repetition
rationale.norman_balance: Strong reflective concept and decent visceral charm, but behavioral usability suffers because the dense micro-charts resist quick reading.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—the morning-peak / post-lunch-valley topography is clearly legible at a glance, fulfilling the brief's metaphor.
